title: Delivery Terms for Stocked Pantries under the Office Pantry & Beverage Program
content:
Standing deliveries to an Office Pantry & Beverage Program pantry are made on the weekday recorded on the programme, at the number of visits a week and within the window printed against the tier. The terms below govern the standing pattern, changes to it, shortages and work asked for outside the schedule.

## Standing deliveries

1. Deliveries are only made while the programme stands active; a paused programme takes no delivery, and a closed programme takes none at all. The status standing on the programme is read from Larkspur Table's own record of that programme before a delivery is made, alongside the delivery weekday recorded on it.
2. The contents of a delivery are fixed the number of hours before it printed against the tier, and a change asked for later than that is made on the following delivery instead.
3. Where a product on the standing list is short, it is substituted with an equivalent up to the substitution share printed against the tier; beyond that share the delivery is made short and the shortfall is credited.

## Deliveries asked for outside the standing pattern

4. An unscheduled replenishment asked for by the client carries the rush delivery charge printed against the tier and is only accepted at or beyond the rush lead hours printed against the same tier.
5. An emergency restock outside the delivery schedule carries the call-out charge printed against the tier, and is distinct from a rush replenishment because it is unplanned on both sides.

## Fresh items

6. Fresh items are delivered only on tiers whose fresh product count is above zero, and a client asking for fresh items on a tier without them is offered the tier that carries them.

## The status test, branch by branch

| Status standing on the programme | Is a standing delivery made |
| --- | --- |
| active | yes |
| paused | no |
| closed | no |

## Points of judgement

Question: a change to the contents of a delivery reaches the desk after the hours printed against the tier have run down.
Answer: the contents of that delivery stand fixed, and the change is made on the following delivery instead.

Question: a product on the standing list is short by more than the substitution share printed against the tier.
Answer: substitution with an equivalent covers the share printed against the tier; the delivery is made short beyond it, and the shortfall is credited.

Question: the client asks for an unscheduled replenishment at shorter notice than the rush lead hours printed against their tier.
Answer: an unscheduled replenishment is accepted at or beyond those hours, so notice at the printed figure itself is accepted and notice shorter than it is not.
